title: Sesterce plans a €10B AI campus in Jämsä
content:
Company ·
Sesterce Plans a €10 Billion AI Campus in Jämsä
A planned investment of over €10 billion would bring AI infrastructure to the former Kaipola paper mill, starting with a 200 MW first phase.
Jämsä, Finland — October 8, 2026. Sesterce is planning a large-scale Sesterce Campus on the site of the former Kaipola paper mill. The investment of over €10 billion aims to create a renewable-powered European AI campus and strengthen Europe’s digital infrastructure and competitiveness.
A new chapter for the Kaipola industrial site
The project will develop supercomputing and computing infrastructure for artificial intelligence on an existing industrial site. It is expected to significantly strengthen the economic vitality of the area.
During construction, the project is expected to employ approximately 2,000 people, and around 300 people once the campus is fully operational. Sesterce is committed to working primarily with Finnish contractors and subcontractors for construction.
“For more than six decades, the Kaipola mill produced paper for the world. Now, a new generation of industry is being planned for the site. Our goal is to preserve the area's industrial identity while making use of existing infrastructure, including the power grid, water systems, buildings and logistics connections.”
Youssef El Manssouri, CEO of Sesterce
A phased development, starting at 200 MW
The first phase, with works planned to start in 2026, will have a capacity of 200 MW. Capacity is expected to increase to 600 MW in the second phase.
Over the longer term, Sesterce aims to build more than one gigawatt of AI capacity in Finland, on existing industrial sites and in line with real market demand.
The project is based on real demand and committed workload capacity: Sesterce already has an anchor customer and a strong outlook for the gradual growth of computing demand.
Four commitments for the Jämsä campus
Each Sesterce Campus commitment will be measured, audited by an independent third party and reported publicly every year.
New renewable capacity for the Finnish grid
For every 1 MW consumed by the campus, Sesterce commits to enabling 1 MW of new renewable generation capacity within the Finnish power grid, within ten years of the campus becoming operational. Only newly built generation capacity will qualify.
No drinking water for cooling
Cooling will rely on a closed-loop liquid system, supplemented with harvested rainwater and recycled water. Drinking water will not be used for cooling.
A €10 million community fund
Upon commissioning of the Jämsä campus, Sesterce will establish a €10 million community fund to finance local projects selected by the City of Jämsä together with local residents.
A campus open to its community
The site will include facilities open to the public, such as restaurants and education and learning spaces. The facilities serving the AI infrastructure will remain separate, secure and protected.
Energy-efficient and flexible operations
“Our planning is based on energy-efficient and flexible operations. The Sesterce Campus projects will use liquid cooling, deliver high energy efficiency and feature controllable and flexible power consumption. Opportunities for utilizing waste heat are also being considered as part of the design.”
Youssef El Manssouri, CEO of Sesterce
This operating model supports the long-term development of Finland’s electricity grid and investment planning. Sesterce is also actively exploring further opportunities for industrial site redevelopment across Finland.
Perspectives from Jämsä and Elenia
Jori Reijula, Mayor of Jämsä
“Jämsä needs new investments, business activity and jobs. The Sesterce project is an interesting opportunity to strengthen the vitality of the region, provided it progresses from plans to implementation and meets the applicable requirements. The redevelopment of the Kaipola site would be a welcome opportunity to give the area a new lease on life and support job creation in Jämsä. The City wants to advance investment projects in cooperation with businesses and will assess each project carefully as it moves forward.”
Jorma Myllymäki, CEO of Elenia
“A functioning, reliable and resilient electricity network is a key enabler of vitality, economic growth, and large-scale industrial investments. The Kaipola industrial site is connected to Elenia's high-voltage electricity network, which currently provides a solid foundation for implementing the first phase of the project.”
About Sesterce
Sesterce is a French AI infrastructure company that develops and operates computing capacity for artificial intelligence. Through its Sesterce Campus model, it develops renewable-powered AI campuses designed with and for their communities. The group has entities in France, the United States and Singapore.

report.summary: Sesterce plans over €10B AI campus at former Kaipola paper mill in Jämsä, Finland, starting with 200 MW and renewable-powered capacity.
report.background: Europe is racing to expand AI compute capacity while facing grid constraints, energy costs, and dependence on US and Asian cloud providers. Finland offers cheap renewable power, cool climate, and industrial sites with existing grid and water infrastructure. Sesterce, a French AI infrastructure company, is repurposing the closed Kaipola paper mill to build a renewable-powered AI campus. The project reflects a broader trend of converting legacy industrial sites into data centers, driven by AI demand for GPU clusters, sovereign AI goals, and the need for flexible, energy-efficient operations. The phased plan begins at 200 MW, with long-term ambitions above one gigawatt in Finland, contingent on real market demand and an anchor customer.
key_points: Sesterce plans a €10 billion AI campus at the former Kaipola paper mill in Jämsä, Finland. Phase one is 200 MW, planned to start in 2026, rising to 600 MW in phase two, with long-term ambitions above one gigawatt across Finnish industrial sites, based on committed demand and an anchor customer.

The project reuses existing industrial infrastructure, including power grid, water systems, buildings, and logistics connections. Construction is expected to employ about 2,000 people, with around 300 permanent roles once operational. Sesterce says it will work primarily with Finnish contractors and subcontractors.

Sustainability commitments include enabling 1 MW of new renewable generation for every 1 MW consumed within ten years, using closed-loop liquid cooling with harvested rainwater and recycled water, and avoiding drinking water for cooling. Waste heat utilization is also being considered.

Governance includes a €10 million community fund upon commissioning, public-facing facilities such as restaurants and learning spaces, and annual independent audits of campus commitments. The secure AI infrastructure remains separate from public areas.

Operationally, the campus emphasizes liquid cooling, high energy efficiency, and flexible, controllable power consumption. Elenia’s high-voltage network supports phase one. Jämsä’s mayor welcomes the plan cautiously, pending permits, implementation, and local benefits.
report.impact: For the AI industry, this signals a shift toward massive, renewable-powered European compute campuses built on legacy industrial sites, reducing reliance on US hyperscalers and supporting sovereign AI ambitions. Developers could gain more regional GPU capacity, potentially lowering latency and compliance friction for European AI workloads. For regular users, it may bring local jobs and community funds, but also raises questions about electricity demand, water use, and grid strain. Success depends on financing, permits, power availability, and whether AI demand grows as projected. If replicated, it could reshape Europe’s AI infrastructure map and accelerate competitive pressure on cloud pricing and sustainability standards.
